# Virology and Outbreak Procedure
1. On discovery of a contagious illness, isolate symptomatic patients and don appropriate PPE before extended contact. 2. Collect swabs for rapid surface/mucosal screening and blood samples for centrifuged panels when stage, antibodies, or systemic involvement must be confirmed. 3. Virology airlocks should be cycled closed to sterilize chamber air and decontaminate exposed gear when leaving the lab. 4. Quarantine may be ordered by the CMO. Release from quarantine requires resolved symptoms and, when available, a negative follow-up test or documented immunity/vaccine status. 5. Medical may request Code Violet when an outbreak threatens station-wide spread or overwhelms medical capacity. See Violet Alert Protocol. 6. Naturally occurring outbreaks are handled as medical incidents. Suspected deliberate release (food contamination, atmos distribution, engineered strains) requires Security involvement and evidence preservation. 7. Live pathogen experimentation and intentional environmental release are prohibited outside authorized containment. 8. Between-patient surgical hygiene is mandatory on virology-enabled stations: sterile/disinfected tools, mask and gloves, and wound preparation.
